newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Shooting signals "unstable" Korean situation - Cohen.
newsitem.headline: Shooting signals "unstable" Korean situation - Cohen.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen said a shooting incident in the Demilitarized Zone between North and South Korea on Thursday confirmed that the peninsula remained in a "dangerous, unstable situation".
"It confirms that it is still a very tense, dangerous, unstable situation as far as the North Koreans are concerned," he told reporters. "We have to be vigilant."

North and South Korean troops exchanged warning shots at their tense border earlier on Thursday about an hour before Cohen visited the Demilitarized Zone about 100 km (60 miles) west of the flashpoint, a Seoul military spokesman said.

In the interview with reporters travelling with him on an Asian visit, Cohen said that while the shooting was not something unexpected, there had been "relatively little provocation" in recent weeks and months from the North Korean military.

"There has been little provocation since the submarine incident and so this comes as a somtheing of a break in that period of calm," he said, referring to the grounding of a North Korean submarine off South Korea last September.
"Now whether that is an isolated situation or is a foreboding of things to come remains to be seen," Cohen said. "I think they (U.S. and South Korean military) will watch it very closely."
